memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The family heads of the clan of Gilead son of Makir, the son of Manasseh, who were from the clans of the descendants of Joseph, came and spoke before Moses and the leaders, the heads of the Israelite families. They said, "When the Lord commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance to the Israelites by lot, he ordered you to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters." - Num 36:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The final chapter of Numbers opens with a group of family leaders bringing a genuine concern to Moses. Earlier, the five daughters of Zelophehad had come forward asking to inherit their father's land, since he had no sons, and God had granted their request (Num 27). Now the leaders of their clan raise a follow-up question about how that ruling might affect the wider tribe. Notice how they came — respectfully, acknowledging what the Lord had commanded, seeking a right resolution rather than stirring up conflict.

There is wisdom in the way they approached this. They did not grumble behind Moses' back or resist God's earlier decision. They came openly, humbly, and constructively, wanting to honour both the daughters' inheritance and the good of the whole tribe. When we have honest concerns, this is the model to follow — bringing them into the light with humility and respect, seeking God's wisdom rather than pushing our own agenda.

How different our communities and families would be if we handled our concerns this way. So often we complain rather than communicate, or we let resentment simmer instead of seeking resolution. God honours those who come to Him and to one another with humble, honest hearts.

This also shows us a God who welcomes our questions. He is not threatened by our sincere concerns. Just as He heard the daughters' request and now hears the clan's follow-up, He invites us to bring our real questions to Him. We can approach the throne of grace with confidence (Heb 4:16), trusting that God listens and responds with wisdom to those who come humbly seeking His way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you typically handle your concerns — with humble honesty or with grumbling?
2. Is there a matter you need to bring openly into the light rather than letting it simmer?
3. How does knowing God welcomes your honest questions encourage you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to bring my concerns humbly and honestly, seeking Your wisdom rather than my own way. Thank You that You welcome my questions and respond with grace. Amen.
